body.title: fix(binarymgr): write install progress to stderr
body.description:
## Description

Install and download progress from the binary manager (for example the first run of `glab orbit`) was written to stdout. Redirecting a command, like `glab orbit --yes skills get orbit > SKILL.md`, put those progress lines into the output file. Progress and status messages now go to stderr, so stdout carries only the command's own output.

## Related Issues

No project issue yet.

## How has this been tested?

`go test ./internal/binarymgr/... ./internal/commands/orbit/...` and `golangci-lint run ./internal/binarymgr/...`. The checksum and below-minimum-version tests assert stdout stays empty and the message lands on stderr. A new `HandleInstall` test runs the full download and install against a mocked registry and checks that stdout is empty while stderr has the progress lines.

<details>
<summary>Agent context</summary>

- `manager.go`: download, checksum, and installed-path messages switched from `LogInfof` to `LogErrorf`.
- `runner.go`: the custom-binary notice on the run path, the "No version installed" line in update, the below-minimum-version warning, and the warning helper also go to stderr.
- Left on stdout: results of explicit `install`/`update` commands (for example "already installed", "Successfully updated"), because those are the command's own output.

</details>

body.title: docs: fix dead handbook and docs links in contributor docs
body.description:
## Description

Seven links in the contributor and maintainer docs point to pages that moved. The handbook links return 404, the release docs link redirects to the root of the `release/docs` repository, and two docs.gitlab.com links use anchors that no longer exist on the page. This MR points each one at the current page. Only URLs change.

| File | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/maintainer.md` (2 links) | `handbook/business-technology/end-user-services/onboarding-access-requests/access-requests/` (404) | `handbook/eta/corporate-it/end-user-services/access-requests/` |
| `docs/triaging_bugs.md` | `handbook/engineering/infrastructure/engineering-productivity/issue-triage/#severity` (404) | `handbook/product-development/how-we-work/issue-triage/#severity` |
| `SECURITY.md` | `handbook/security/product-security/application-security/vulnerability-management/#vulnerability-vs-feature-vs-bug` (404) | `handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/application-security/vulnerability-management/#vulnerability-vs-feature-vs-bug` |
| `docs/security_releases.md` | `release/docs/-/blob/master/general/security/developer.md` (file renamed) | `release/docs/-/blob/master/general/security/engineer.md` |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | `cli_styleguide/#deprecation-messages` (no such anchor) | `cli_styleguide/#deprecations` |
| `docs/development_process.md` | `automatic_reviewer_assignment/#assign-reviewers-with-the-recommend-reviewers-flow` (no such anchor) | `automatic_reviewer_assignment/#recommend-reviewers-flow` |

Each new page covers the same topic as the old link: the Access Requests page, the Issue Triage page with its Severity section, the Application Vulnerability Management Procedure with its "Vulnerability vs. Feature vs. Bug?" section, the release docs engineer guide (`developer.md` was renamed to `engineer.md` in `release/docs@6f229680`), the CLI style guide Deprecations section, and the Recommend Reviewers flow section.

## Related issues and merge requests

None.

## Documentation

No CLI command docs change, so `make gen-docs` is not needed.

## How was this checked?

- `curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}'` on each old URL: 404 for the three handbook links; the `developer.md` link ends at `release/docs/-/tree/master`.
- Same command on each new URL: 200. Each `#anchor` is an `id` in the live page HTML.
- `release/docs` commit `6f229680` renames `general/security/developer.md` to `general/security/engineer.md`.

This contribution was prepared with the help of an AI assistant. I reviewed the changes and take responsibility for them.

body.title: chore(deps): replace mgutz/ansi with local SGR codes
body.description:
## Description

`github.com/mgutz/ansi` is unmaintained, and its only remaining use was the basic-ANSI fallback in `makeColorFunc` (`internal/iostreams/color.go`). This MR replaces that call with a small map from the eight palette names to their SGR parameters, then drops the dependency (`go mod tidy`). Nothing else in the module graph imports it.

- Output is byte-identical to what mgutz/ansi produced. I checked each name against the library directly, for example `default+b` gives `\x1b[0;1;39m…\x1b[0m`.
- Empty input still returns `""`, as before.
- An unknown name now returns the text unchanged. mgutz/ansi fell back to black (`0;30`) in that case. All callers pass one of the eight fixed names, so this path never runs.
- The issue suggests `termenv`. I didn't use it here because the closed !3141 lost color under the pager: `termenv` probes `s.StdOut` for a TTY, and under the pager that is a pipe. Writing the codes directly keeps the current TTY and color gating as it is.
- I also removed the `// basic ANSI colors` comment, because `scripts/comment-overlap` flags it against the new lookup line.

Note: !3955 also edits `makeColorFunc` and `color_test.go`. This diff stays small so that whichever MR merges second only has a small rebase.

## Related Issues

Resolves https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8270

## How has this been tested?

- `Test_makeColorFunc`: the existing cases pass unchanged. I added table cases for magenta, cyan, red, yellow, blue, `default+b` and an unknown name, plus a test for empty text.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/iostreams/...` reports 0 issues.

body.description:
## Description

Coding agents prompted with just "use Orbit" don't know it maps to `glab orbit`. The `orbit` row in `glab --help` now says it queries the GitLab Orbit context graph. The help shown before the binary is downloaded points agents to the skill command with `--yes`, so the first install doesn't prompt.

## Related Issues

No project issue; this is a small follow-up to the Orbit CLI help text.

## How has this been tested?

`go test ./internal/commands/orbit/...`, with the help test extended to check the `--yes` pointer. Docs regenerated with `make gen-docs`.

<details>
<summary>Agent context</summary>

- Changed `Short` and `Long` in `internal/commands/orbit/orbit.go`; `README.md` and `docs/source/orbit/_index.md` regenerated.
- The pre-install fallback help prints `Long`, so no separate code path was needed.
- Labels come from the default MR template plus `type::maintenance`; the milestone is 19.6.

</details>

## Before and after

`glab --help` row:

```plaintext
before: Run the GitLab Orbit CLI. (EXPERIMENTAL)
after:  Query the GitLab Orbit context graph. (EXPERIMENTAL)
```

New paragraph in `glab orbit --help` before the binary is installed:

```plaintext
Coding agents: run `glab orbit --yes skills get orbit` to load the Orbit skill. `--yes` installs the binary without a prompt on first use.
```

body.title: feat(mr): respect --push=false with --fill
body.description:
## Description

`glab mr create --fill` always pushes the source branch, and an explicit `--push=false` is ignored: the autofill branch of `run()` sets `ShouldPush = true` after the flags are parsed, so the value given on the command line never reaches the push. That leaves no way to use `--fill` when the push itself fails, which is the case in the issue: a Jujutsu bookmark pushed by an earlier step, where pushing `HEAD` again conflicts with the remote and aborts the command.

This MR follows the plan in the issue, in four commits:

1. `test(mr): pin that mr create --fill pushes the source branch` adds `TestNewCmdCreate_FillPush`. It drives the command through `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` with `--fill` and with `--fill --push`, and asserts on the `git` commands the command stubber records: one `git push origin HEAD:feat-new-mr` each. Nothing ran `--fill` through to the push before. Both cases pass on `main`.
2. `feat(mr): respect --push=false with --fill` is the fix. `complete()` records whether `--push` was given, with `cmd.Flags().Changed("push")`, after the handling of `--allow-collaboration`, `--remove-source-branch` and `--squash-before-merge`, and the autofill branch turns the push on only when it was not. Bare `--fill` and `--fill --push` push as before, and `--fill --push=false` creates the merge request without pushing. The commit adds that third case to the test, which fails on the first commit and passes on this one.
3. `docs(mr): describe --push=false with --fill in mr create help`. The `--fill` description wrapped `push` in backticks, which pflag reads as the flag's value name, so the help and `docs/source/mr/create.md` showed `-f, --fill push`. It now says the branch is pushed unless `--push=false` is set. The `--push` description says it defaults to true with `--fill` and that `--push=false` skips the push, and there is an example for `--fill --push=false`.
4. `docs(mr): say that mr create --push pushes before creating`. The `--push` description said the push happens after the merge request is created, while `run()` pushes first and creates the merge request afterwards.

Commits 3 and 4 carry `docs/source/mr/create.md` exactly as `make gen-docs` writes it.

Step 5 of the plan, the error when the branch is not on the remote: GitLab refuses the create with `400 {"message":{"source_branch":["does not exist"]}}` (the spec "returns 400 when source_branch does not exist in the repository" in `spec/requests/api/merge_requests_spec.rb` pins that answer), and against the stub described below, glab prints:

```plaintext
Post http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/v4/projects/OWNER%2FREPO/merge_requests: 400 {message: {source_branch: [does not exist]}}.
```

It names the field and what is wrong with it, and it is the error `glab mr create` already gives today without `--fill` for a branch that was never pushed, so I left it as it is. If you would rather have a hint that points at `--push` there, I can add it to this MR.

## Related Issues

Closes gitlab-org/cli#8224

## How has this been tested?

With Go 1.27.2 and golangci-lint 2.14.0, on each of the four commits:

- `TestNewCmdCreate_FillPush` passes. On the first commit, the `--push=false` case added by the second fails with `expected: [][]string(nil)`, `actual: [][]string{[]string{"git", "push", "origin", "HEAD:feat-new-mr"}}`, and the other two pass.
- `go test` passes on the packages `make test-changed` selects for this change, the changed package and every package that imports it: `cmd/gen-docs`, `cmd/glab`, `internal/commands`, `internal/commands/mr`, `internal/commands/mr/create`, `internal/commands/stack` and `internal/commands/stack/sync`.
- `golangci-lint run` (`make lint`): 0 issues. `golangci-lint fmt --diff`, `go vet ./internal/commands/mr/...`, `make check-embed check-args` and `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0 ./cmd/... ./internal/...` are clean.
- `go run ./cmd/gen-docs/docs.go`, which is what `make gen-docs` runs, leaves `docs/` and `README.md` unchanged.
- On commits 3 and 4, in the docs lint image CI uses, `vale --minAlertLevel error`, `markdownlint-cli2` and `lychee --offline --include-fragments` report nothing on `docs/source/mr/create.md`.
- Every commit message and the title pass commitlint with `scripts/commit-lint/.commitlintrc.js`.

End to end, I built glab from `main` and from this branch and ran both in a scratch repository whose `origin` is a small stub of the GitLab API. The stub logs every request, git's smart HTTP requests included, so a push attempt shows up as `GET /OWNER/REPO.git/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`. `feat-on-remote` is a branch the stub reports as present, `feat-local-only` one it does not.

<details>
<summary>Runs and the stub's request log</summary>


body.title: fix(auth): fail clearly on a missing keyring token
body.description:
## Description

When a host has `use_keyring: "true"` but its keyring entry is gone, glab sent requests without a token. Every command ended in a bare `401 Unauthorized`, with no hint about the missing credential. Now glab stops before the request, with the same kind of error OAuth hosts already get:

```plaintext
the token for "gitlab.example.com" is missing from the operating system keyring; run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.example.com` to re-authenticate
```

Decisions, by their effect on users:

1. A token from `GITLAB_TOKEN`, the plaintext config, or a CI job token still wins. The error only shows when there is no token at all.
2. Only `use_keyring` in the host's own config entry counts. A top-level `use_keyring` (from `glab config set use_keyring true --global`) and `GLAB_USE_KEYRING` do not, the same as when glab reads the token. Otherwise, they would make every tokenless host fail.
3. `glab auth login --web` and `--device` save `use_keyring` before any token exists, so the first login would hit the new error. That login step now does not read or send a token, so a locked keyring does not block it either. It keeps the host's proxy, CA, client certificate, `skip_tls_verify` and `api_host` settings.
4. This also fixes a re-login loop. If an OAuth host's keyring entries are gone, `glab auth login --device` on `main` fails and tells you to run `glab auth login`. On this branch, the login starts.

Behavior changes on a host with `use_keyring: "true"` and no keyring entry:

- Anonymous reads (for example on public projects) now fail early with the error above.
- `glab auth docker-helper` still works for registries on other hosts, because it does not need the default host's token. A registry on this host still fails, and for an Artifact Registry the error is the one above.

## Related Issues

Related to #8552

I didn't use `Closes`. I fixed the bug the maintainer described in the issue:

> when a host is configured with `use_keyring: true` and the keyring entry is missing, glab treats the token as unset and builds an unauthenticated client, so the result is a bare 401 with nothing pointing back at the credential. The OAuth2 path already fails with an actionable message in that situation; the personal access token path does not.

The reporter's own 401 may come from how `glab api` and `glab auth status` pick the host. That question is still open, so I left the issue open.

## How has this been tested?

I built `glab` from `main` and from this branch. I used a temporary config with `use_keyring: "true"` for a local stub server, and no keyring entry.

```plaintext
$ glab api user        # built from main
{"message": "401 Unauthorized"}glab: 401 Unauthorized (HTTP 401)

$ glab api user        # built from this branch
  The token for "127.0.0.1:18552" is missing from the operating system keyring; run `glab auth login --hostname
  127.0.0.1:18552` to re-authenticate.
```

Then I removed `use_keyring` from the host entry and ran `glab config set use_keyring true --global`. The previous commit of this branch stopped with the keyring error here. Now the request goes out:

```plaintext
$ glab api user        # built from this branch
{"message": "401 Unauthorized"}glab: 401 Unauthorized (HTTP 401)

$ GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-stub glab api user        # built from this branch
{"id": 1, "username": "stub-user", "name": "Stub"}
```

For decision 3, I ran `glab auth login --device` for a new host. Both builds reached the device endpoint. A branch build with the old login code stopped with the new error instead. For decision 4, `main` failed with `Oauth2 authentication is configured ... run glab auth login`, and the branch reached the device endpoint.

I added unit tests for the new error, an environment token, a job token, `GLAB_USE_KEYRING`, and the login step keeping TLS and header settings. After the review, I added tests for `--device` with no stored token, a locked keyring when the login client skips the token, the Docker helper with a tokenless default host, and a tokenless host under a top-level `use_keyring`. Each of these fails on the code before the fix.

```shell
$ go test -count=1 ./internal/api/ ./internal/config/ ./internal/commands/auth/docker/ ./internal/commands/auth/login/ ./internal/commands/auth/status/
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/api	0.419s
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/config	2.242s
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/auth/docker	0.261s
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/auth/login	38.528s
ok  	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/auth/status	0.030s
```

`gofmt -s -l`, `gofumpt -l` and `go vet` printed nothing. `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev` on the changed packages reported 0 issues. The rest runs in the pipeline.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

Not applicable, the change is in CLI output. The new error text is above.

Implemented with AI assistance; I reviewed and tested the changes.

body.title: fix(issue): show the real total in the list header
body.description:
## Description

`glab issue list` and `glab incident list` discarded the `*gitlab.Response`
from `ListProjectIssues` and `ListGroupIssues`, so the header only reported the
number of rows on the current page. With the default page size there was no way
to tell that more issues existed.

This keeps the response and passes `resp.TotalItems` to the list title, the same
approach as !3991 (`label list`) and !4015 (`iteration list`):

- The header reads, for example,
  `Showing 30 of 120 open issues in OWNER/REPO that match your search. (Page 1)`.
- When the response carries no total (GitLab omits `X-Total` for very large
  result sets), the header stays as it is today.
- `--epic` keeps the page count. Epic issues are filtered client-side, so the
  API total would not match the rows shown.

Only the header line changes. The table, `--output json`, and
`--output-format ids|urls` are unchanged.

This is the first of the per-command MRs announced in
https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/1165#note_3988459828.
`schedule list` and `mr list` follow separately. Step 1 of the implementation
plan in #1165 (`(Page N of M)` and the next-page hint) is not part of this MR,
because it changes the header of every list command.

!3256 rewrites the same project branch of `listRun` (the `ListProjectIssues`
call), so whichever of the two lands second will need a small rebase.

## Related Issues

Related to #1165

## How has this been tested?

- `internal/commands/issuable/list/issuable_list_test.go`: added
  `TestIssueList_headerTotal` with five cases:
  - project, group (`--page 21`), and incident responses with a total expect
    `of 42` / `of 5`. These three fail on `main`.
  - a response without a total keeps `Showing 2 open issues ...`.
